This audit is excellent — thank you for the repro scripts, they made independent verification straightforward.

I re-verified several of these against current `main` (`f1ade81`) before touching anything, and opened #40 for **bugs 2 and 8**, which share a root cause worth stating plainly: absence of evidence was being scored as agreement. Two 30x30 subjects at opposite corners of a 200x200 frame share zero pixels and report `silhouetteIoU 1.0, passed: true, failures: []`.

Status of the rest, as I found it:

- **Bug 1 (scale hard gate / key mismatch) — already fixed** on current `main`. Your report was filed against `7b1c62c`; `divine_eye.py:290-291` now reads the snake_case keys and carries a comment explaining the original defect. Worth striking from the list.
- **Bug 2 — fixed in #40.** Both `load_mask` callers discarded the inversion warning; `diagnose_render_multi_angle.py:52` already handled it correctly, so the right pattern existed in-repo.
- **Bug 8 — fixed in #40.** Empty union now scores `0.0` in both `silhouette_iou` and `edge_overlap`.
- **Bug 4 — confirmed still live,** with one refinement to your description: plain `validate_sculpt_spec.py` returns **0** on a profile-less lathe. `--strict-quality` does return 1, but on unrelated starter-spec warnings, not the missing profile — so neither validator actually catches it. The generator then exits 0 emitting the default hourglass with no marker, four lines below the docstring promising *"Never silently substitute a box... with no signal that anything was wrong."*
- **Bugs 3 and 5 — confirmed still live** by inspection. The weighted ensemble is entirely luma/shape derived, and `make_character_component_tree(anatomy)` never references its `anatomy` parameter.

You offered to send PRs for these — I've deliberately taken only 2 and 8 so as not to cut across your work. Happy to pick up bug 4 if you'd rather not, or to leave it entirely; just say which. Bugs 3 and 5 change scoring and template semantics, so those probably deserve a maintainer design call before anyone writes code.

I reproduced the conflict locally to see what's actually blocking this, since it's been sitting a few days. Good news first: **`export/glbExporter.js` merges cleanly.** All 909 lines of the actual feature are fine, and `SKILL.md` and `README.md` auto-merge. Only two files conflict, and both are bookkeeping:

```
Auto-merging SKILL.md          OK
Auto-merging README.md         OK
CONFLICT (content): CHANGELOG.md
CONFLICT (content): ROADMAP.md
```

**`CHANGELOG.md` is mechanical.** This PR adds an `## [Unreleased]` block; `main` has since added `[1.4.1]` and `[1.4.0]`. `main` has no `[Unreleased]` section at all, so nothing is being overwritten — keep both, with `[Unreleased]` sitting above `[1.4.1]`. That's the same ordering fix @risha-max already did once for the 1.3 merge.

**`ROADMAP.md` needs a decision, not just a resolution** — this is the part I think is worth flagging, because the roadmap was rewritten underneath this PR by #26 ("one theme per release"):

- This branch adds `### v1.4 - Animation-ready rigs`
- On current `main`, **v1.4 is "The Weapon Update", already shipped 2026-07-25–26**, and the rig content moved to `### v1.5 — The Character Update`

So re-resolving that hunk textually would reintroduce a v1.4 section that no longer describes v1.4.

The useful part: **`main`'s roadmap already has a home for this work.** `ROADMAP.md:176`:

```
| G2 | glTF / GLB export + AnimationMixer (engine portability) | Roadmap v1.7 — Game Pipeline | deferred |
```

This PR ships the model-level half of G2. So the smaller and more accurate edit is probably to update that row (deferred → model-level export landed via the viewer, AnimationMixer still pending) and drop the new roadmap section entirely, rather than re-adding a v1.4 heading. That also shrinks the diff to the point where the CHANGELOG hunk is the only thing left.

Not trying to step on this — it's @juancamusss's feature and @risha-max's rebase, and you both know the export code far better than I do. Just wanted the conflict to be a 10-minute fix instead of an unknown. If a second pair of hands would help I'm happy to push the resolution to a branch for you to cherry-pick, but only if you'd rather not do it yourselves.

## Review: request changes

I found two actionable installer defects.

### High: --target paths containing spaces are split

TARGETS is stored as a space-delimited string and later iterated unquoted in install.sh. A command such as: ./install.sh --target "/tmp/target with spaces" exits successfully but creates separate unintended paths instead of installing under the requested directory.

Relevant lines: install.sh:50-64,155-160. Please preserve each target as one argument and add regression coverage for spaced and repeated targets.

### High: uninstall ownership check is too weak

--uninstall only checks for SKILL.md, forge/, and grimoire/ before recursively removing the directory. Any directory with those markers can be deleted, even if it was not installed by this script.

Relevant lines: install.sh:90-92,114-120. Please verify stronger installer ownership before deletion and add a regression test.

Verification update for the PS5/DualSense multi-view pipeline:

- Re-ran the pipeline with all six reference views: top, front, back, bottom, left, and right.
- Intake correctly selected full synthesis mode and preserved all six source images through the assessment and generated sculpt spec. It reported evidence-only confidence of 0.49, which is expected without calibrated camera data.
- Performance check: 1.21s cold run and 0.04s warm run.
- Full test suite passed: 307 tests. The production build also passed.
- The multi-angle volume gate passed, so the render set is not a flat or billboard reconstruction.
- The actual six-pair Divine Eye review completed with no missing views and correctly failed closed: aggregate fidelity 0.299 against the 0.85 target; all six views were rejected on silhouette and/or scale hard gates. This confirms that multi-view ingestion and review gating work as intended, while the current PS5 reconstruction still needs refine-code work.
- Note: Divine Eye did not complete on the original 1536px images (empty output); the deterministic review was therefore run on isolated 512px review copies. This should be tracked as a full-resolution memory/performance concern.

No source-code changes were made as part of this validation run.

### Re-test at `c343dbf`

Re-ran the same eight-view subject from the `abd3e30` field test. Most of what I raised is closed, and the view-classification fix is confirmed by measurement rather than by reading the diff.

**View classification — fixed.** Same eight files, same call:

```
abd3e30  front, front-2, front-3, front-4, front-5, front-6, back, view-side-elevation
c343dbf  front, front-2, three-quarter-front-right x4, back, side
```

All four three-quarter plates now classify correctly, bare `side` is recognised instead of falling through to the raw filename, and `viewCount` goes 3 -> 4 because an elevation is no longer collapsed with an oblique. `THREE_QUARTER_ALIASES` plus collecting every matched direction instead of returning on the first is the right shape of fix.

**Also closed:**
- the `stage1b -> stage4` back-edge is gone from `review_enhancer.py`
- `SKILL.md` now routes multi-view work (lines 78, 99) — `grep -ci "multi-view\|stage1b"` was 0 at `abd3e30`
- `multi_view_analysis.md` gained `### Contradictory Views` with a metric authority, conflicts recorded as explicit assumptions, and `request-input` when nothing can reconcile them
- quality gates split into evidence-only vs calibrated metric envelope, so the checklist is satisfiable in the mode the module actually ships in

**Independent corroboration for the Contradictory Views section.** I ran two further agents on the same eight plates, each isolated, each blocked from reading the others' output. All three reconstructions hit the same wall and none could resolve it:

- run A: front elevation implies ~8.8 m depth, flank implies ~11 m — took 8.25
- run B: *"none of the four three-quarter plates can be reproduced at [10.1 m]"* — took 9.0
- run C: *"iso views imply ~6.7 m; the side elevation implies ~11 m"* — split the difference

Run C found two more the others missed: the front elevation draws the upper ridge 0.6 m left of centre while rear and isos centre it, and `view-front-elevation.png` is near-orthographic while `-b` shows real perspective, so the two disagree about how much roof an elevation should show. Three independent builders, three different resolutions, same underlying contradiction — that section is load-bearing.

**Two still open:**

1. `feature_detector.py` still carries three `import cv2` sites (plus `feature_matcher.py`, `pose_estimator.py`) against `CONTRIBUTING.md:28`. It fails closed correctly, so behaviour is honest, but the metric path never runs and `poseConfidence` stays at 0.02.
2. `synthesize.py:174` still computes `duplicateViewCount` as `input_view_count - view_count`. It improved from 5 to 4 purely because the naming fix reduced collapsing — but it is still counting views lost to grouping, not duplicates. `check_reference_admission.py` rejects exactly 1 on this set.

Validation: `python3 -m unittest discover -s forge/tests` passes on `c343dbf`; multi-view synthesis re-run on the eight-view set above.

Note: unrelated to this PR but found on the same subject — `diagnose_render.py:108` destructures the bboxes as `_rx, _ry, rw, rh`, so scale and aspect are translation-invariant and nothing measures centroid offset. On run C that cost silhouette IoU 0.653 against 0.869 after registration, and it misattributed the gap to the ink-outlined references. Runs A and B, which registered first, both cleared the gate. I will raise that separately.

## PR Review: Cross-Agent Resumable State Foundation

**Verdict**: REQUEST CHANGES | **Critical**: 4 | **Warnings**: 8 | **Improvements**: 12

---

### Critical Issues

#### 1. Path Traversal via Actor Name
**File**: 

An actor name like `../../snapshot` would resolve outside the acknowledgements directory, potentially overwriting other files.

```python
# Current - unsanitized
def acknowledgement_path(self, item_id: ItemId, actor: str) -> Path:
    return self.item_directory(item_id) / "acknowledgements" / f"{actor}.json"

# Fix - validate actor name
import re
ACTOR_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$")
def acknowledgement_path(self, item_id: ItemId, actor: str) -> Path:
    if not ACTOR_PATTERN.fullmatch(actor):
        raise StateProblem("PATH_SECURITY", "actor name contains invalid characters", str(item_id))
    return self.item_directory(item_id) / "acknowledgements" / f"{actor}.json"
```

#### 2. TOCTOU Race in Event Appending
**File**: 

Two concurrent agents can both read `seq=5` and both write `seq=6`, corrupting the ledger. The lease mechanism has a window between expiry and reclaim.

```python
# Fix - use file locking or derive seq from file size
import fcntl
def append_event(self, item_id: ItemId, event: JsonObject) -> JsonObject:
    path = self.events_path(item_id)
    with path.open("ab") as handle:
        fcntl.flock(handle, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        try:
            seq = sum(1 for _ in open(path)) if path.exists() else 0
            event["seq"] = seq
            # ...
        finally:
            fcntl.flock(handle, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
```

#### 3. No Lease TTL — Dead Agent Locks Item Permanently
**File**: 

A crashed agent's lease is indistinguishable from an active one. The only escape is manual file deletion.

```python
# Fix - add TTL check
LEASE_TTL_SECONDS = 300  # 5 minutes
def require_lease(self, item_id: ItemId, actor: str, snapshot: JsonObject) -> JsonObject:
    lease = self.store.read_lease(item_id)
    if not lease or lease.get("actor") != actor:
        raise StateProblem("LEASE_CONFLICT", "active lease for actor is required", str(item_id))
    heartbeat_at = lease.get("heartbeatAt") or lease.get("createdAt")
    if heartbeat_at:
        from datetime import datetime, timezone
        lease_time = datetime.fromisoformat(heartbeat_at)
        if (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - lease_time).total_seconds() > LEASE_TTL_SECONDS:
            raise StateProblem("LEASE_CONFLICT", "lease has expired", str(item_id))
    return lease
```

#### 4. `arguments.json` AttributeError When `--json` Not Passed
**File**: 

`argparse.SUPPRESS` as default means the attribute is never set on Namespace when the flag is absent.

```python
# Fix - use False as default
json_option.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", default=False)
```

---

### Warnings

5. **SCHEMA_VERSION unused** (`model.py:16`) — both `store.py:64` and `service.py:23` hardcode `"1.0"` instead
6. **`release()` unhandled crash** (`service.py:163`) — `unlink()` without `missing_ok=True` raises FileNotFoundError
7. **`commit()` no state machine validation** (`service.py:136`) — accepts arbitrary `next_action` from caller
8. **`initialize()` double-writes** (`service.py:35-37`) — redundant snapshot write after persist
9. **`resume()` reads snapshot twice** (`service.py:67-68`) — wasteful and TOCTOU window
10. **`append_event()` O(n) performance** (`store.py:74`) — reads entire events.jsonl on every append
11. **Hash chain write-only** (`store.py:83-93`) — never verified on read
12. **`list_items()` no pagination** (`service.py:40-50`) — unbounded memory usage

---

| `release` command | ❌ Not tested |

1. `polygonizeSdf`'s quad pass reads `cellAt` out of range at the sampling box's `+X`/`+Y`/`+Z` faces, corrupting the index buffer.

The three quad loops iterate `x`/`y`/`z` over `[0, side)` where `side = resolution + 1` (corner count), but each guard bounds only the *edge* axis (`x + 1 < side`) and the *lower* end of the other two (`y > 0`, `z > 0`). ## 1. `polygonizeSdf` quad pass — confirmed, and reproduced

Correct on all three premises, which I checked in the source before accepting the conclusion: `side = resolution + 1`, `cellVertex` is filled only over `[0, resolution)³`, and there is no bounds padding (`step = (max - min) / resolution` puts the last corner exactly on `max`).

I replicated the indexing in Python against a sphere SDF rather than relying on inspection, and the counts match yours exactly:

| case | out-of-range | aliased |
|---|---|---|
| `resolution=8`, `radius=2.5`, bounds `[-2,2]` | 60 | 108 |
| `resolution=8`, `radius=1.2` (surface inside bounds) | 0 | 0 |

`cellAt(3, 8, 1) == 131` is indeed the slot for cell `(3, 0, 2)`, and `undefined < 0` being `false` is what lets it through the guard in `quad` and into `setIndex`, where it coerces to `0`.

Two notes on the diagnosis:

- My count of `undefined` values reaching `indices` is 60 at `resolution=8` and 200 at `resolution=32`, against your 91 and 300. The out-of-range and aliased counts agree exactly, so this looks like a difference in what we count (per value pushed vs per affected quad) rather than a disagreement about the defect.
- The **aliased** reads are the more dangerous half and a range check cannot see them: `131` is a perfectly valid index, so the quad is silently wired to an unrelated vertex with no error anywhere.

Fixed as you suggested — the missing upper bounds on the two non-edge axes in each of the three loops. After the fix both counts are `0`, and a surface entirely inside its bounds is unchanged (`resolution=24`, `radius=0.6`: 444 triangles before and after), so nothing that previously worked moves.

**Worth stating explicitly for whoever hits this next:** the fix stops the corruption but does not close the mesh. A surface that reaches its sampling box is now left **open** at that face, because the four cells a boundary quad needs genuinely do not all exist. Padding `descriptor.bounds` past the surface is what produces a closed mesh. That is recorded in a comment at the loop.

## Architecture review — measuring this against "everything is a plugin"

Reviewed at `1df8b892`, against `img2/docs/plugin-wiki` and `img2threejs/plugin-cs2`. The direction here is right, and some of the new code is genuinely good — `spec_augmentation.py` uses a deny-list over an allow-list, clamps raise-only, and attributes every accepted change to a provider; `spec_search.content_root` preserves relative-path containment across a second root; `_anchor_index` fails loud instead of appending.

If the target principle is **everything is a plugin**, then that principle is a testable claim, and it implies three things this PR does not yet satisfy:

1. the base holds **zero** domain knowledge,
2. there is **one** plugin surface — the thing we validate is the thing we execute,
3. with no plugin installed, the base is **fully functional**.

Each is currently falsifiable on this branch. Details below, all reproducible.

---

### Blocker: CI is red, and the reason is architectural

Run [32926160364](https://github.com/img2threejs/img2threejs/actions/runs/32926160364) — 2 failures + 1 error.

`registered_domains()` reads `$IMG2_HOME/plugins.json`, and no base test isolates it, so the suite's result depends on machine-global state:

```
IMG2_HOME=$(mktemp -d)         → Ran 9 tests … FAILED (failures=2)
IMG2_HOME=<plugin-cs2 added>   → Ran 9 tests … OK
```

`test_domain_registry.py:35` asserts `sorted(registered_domains()) == ["character","cs2"]` and `:80` expects a `"declared twice"` collision on `cs2` — but the PR ships only `domains/character.py`. They pass only where the plugin happens to be installed. `test_workflow_state.py:58` still calls `new_state(profile="cs2")`.

`test_search_specs.py:243` already sets an empty `IMG2_HOME` for exactly this reason — the pattern exists, it just wasn't applied here.

---

### 1. The base still names the domain it claims to have extracted

`test_the_base_pipeline_names_no_domain` greps two files (`workflow_state.py`, `state.py`) and passes. Five more base modules still name `cs2`:

| module | still holds |
|---|---|
| `stage2_spec/new_pre_spec_assessment.py` | `--cs2`, `CS2_DOMAIN_ID`, `CS2_DETAIL_MINIMUM`, `elif is_character and is_cs2` |
| `stage2_spec/validate_sculpt_spec.py` | `CS2_ROUTES`, `CS2_EXACTNESS_TIERS`, `validate_cs2_contract`, the knife-adapter rule |
| `_shared/pipeline_routing.py` | `classification_from_cs2_manifest`, `legacy_cs2` |
| `stage4_review/append_review.py` | `--cs2-review-json`, `entry["cs2Review"]` |
| `stage3_build/bake_projected_texture.py` | `--manifest` "validated cs2-intake.json" |

Two things stand out. `new_pre_spec_assessment.py:214` is still `elif is_character and is_cs2:` — the exact conditional 01-why calls *"the shape of the whole problem"*. And `CS2_DOMAIN_ID = "cs2"` at `:90` is **added by this PR**, with `:180` having the base write `objectClass["domain"] = "cs2"` from a bare CLI flag — which contradicts `spec_augmentation.py`'s own rule that the marker *"is set by domain resolution, never proposed"*.

Because the base still validates `cs2Intake`, plugin-cs2 currently works by relying on undeclared base coupling in the wrong direction.

Suggestion: widen that test to grep the whole `forge/` tree. It converts the principle from a comment into a gate, and it will fail today — which is the point.

### 2. There are two plugin surfaces, and they don't intersect

A plugin declares itself through five files. Three are read by `img2 doctor` and by nothing else; two drive the run and are validated by nothing.

| file | validated by `doctor` | consumed by `forge/` |
|---|---|---|
| `plugin.json` `capabilities` | yes | **no consumer** |
| `steps.json` | yes | **no consumer** |
| `gates.json` | yes | **no consumer** |
| `domain.json` | **no** — `bin/img2.mjs` never names it | yes, `domains/__init__.py:120` |
| `spec_search_profile.json` | **no** | yes |

Consequences, all currently true:

- **`blocking: true` is decorative.** `gate_runner` is never invoked from the base. Cookbook §289 says *"`blocking: true` stops the workflow"*, plugin-cs2's SKILL.md says *"a failed `cs2-review` blocks continuation"* — `cs2-review` runs only as a `domain.json` checklist row.
- **Typed-edge resolution never runs.** The wiki calls `capabilities` *"the only thing resolution matches on"*; the base resolves by domain id string via `domain_profile(profile)`.
- **`{reference}` in `plugin-cs2/domain.json` passes**, though it's outside the documented closed set and the reference says that *"fails doctor"*. Conversely `domains/__init__.py:131` substitutes only `{plugin_dir}` — so a plugin using the **documented** `{image}` gets an unrendered token.
- **Eleven stanza-less tools pass.** The reference lists 7 grep-enforced tool rules; `staticToolFindings` implements 3. None of plugin-cs2's tools carry the mandatory §8 bootstrap stanza, and 6 of 8 are byte-identical to the deleted base files.

Empirically: `img2 add --link ../plugin-cs2 && img2 doctor` → `ok (1 plugin(s), 0 warning(s))`.

### 3. A plugin is currently load-bearing on the base

> "The base pulls; a plugin never pushes… This is what makes 'no plugin installed' a working path rather than a broken one." — *01-why*

`forge/state.py:30` builds `--profile`'s argparse `choices` from `registered_domains()`, which runs at parser-construction time. A malformed `$IMG2_HOME/plugins.json` — state the base does not own — therefore tracebacks the base CLI, including `--help`:

```
$ IMG2_HOME=<dir with malformed plugins.json> python3 forge/state.py --help
domains.DomainRegistryError: cannot read the plugin registry at …/plugins.json
```

That inverts the principle rather than implementing it. Worth noting `spec_search.py:504` swallows the same corrupt file (`except … return []`) while `domains/__init__.py:127` raises — two different semantics for one file.

### 4. Silent data loss from the flat workspace namespace

Plugin outputs land at the workspace root rather than `<workspace>/.img2/artifacts/<plugin-id>/`, and the new `.gitignore` block enumerates those filenames, which codifies the flat namespace. `admission.json`, `probe.json`, `cs2-intake.json` and `cs2-review.json` also carry no `kind`.

That matters because the checklist passes `--augmentation spec-augmentation.json` for **every** profile, and `new_sculpt_spec.py:1946` joins the augmentation branch and the character template with `elif`:

```
# same assessment, --profile character, run twice on this branch
no augmentation present    → 35 top-level keys
spec-augmentation.json     → 36 top-level keys
                             LOST: ['rig']   gained: ['cs2Finish', 'specAugmentation']
```

`apply_character_template` never runs. Exit 0, plausible-looking spec. Nothing checks the artifact's `provenance.provider` against the resolved domain. This is the failure mode the PR's own rationale names: *"removing either leaves the other unreachable or wrongly reached — and the run still exits 0 with a plausible answer."*

### 5. Two smaller regressions

- **CS2 evidence corpus shrank silently.** The base's old `cs2` collection listed four `distilled_records` including `core_3d.jsonl` and `core_3d_reconstruction.jsonl`. `plugin-cs2/spec_search_profile.json` lists only the two `cs2_*` files, and `content_root` containment (`..` refused) makes the base records unreachable from a plugin collection. Exactly the *"quality loss is invisible"* case the surrounding comment warns about.
- **Duplicate, divergent declarations in plugin-cs2.** `cs2-contract-read` and `cs2-authoritative-classification` appear in both `steps.json` and `domain.json` with different command text; `steps.json` omits `cs2-manifest` and `cs2-spec-augmentation` entirely. `cs2-review` is both a `domain.json` `passStep` and a `gates.json` gate with an identical command — it would run twice per pass once gates are wired.

---

### Converging on "everything is a plugin"

Ordered so each step makes the next one verifiable:

1. **Green the CI** — isolate `$IMG2_HOME` in base tests, rewrite the two registry tests against a fixture domain. Until this lands the suite can't tell us whether anything else worked.
2. **Split the `elif`** in `new_sculpt_spec.py:1946`, and reject an artifact whose `provenance.provider` doesn't match the resolved domain. Silent data loss.
3. **Pick one plugin surface.** Either wire `gate_runner` + capability resolution into the base so `steps.json`/`gates.json`/`capabilities` become live, or drop them and validate `domain.json` instead. Shipping both has plugin authors building against enforcement that doesn't exist.
4. **Finish the extraction** — remove `--cs2` and the CS2 validator from the base, and widen the invariant test to the whole `forge/` tree.
5. **Make `character` a plugin too.** `character.py`'s own docstring argues *"an extension point whose only consumer is one hardcoded in-repo domain is a rename, not an abstraction"* — with cs2 extracted, the seam is back to one in-repo consumer, so that argument now applies to the delivered state. This is also the cleanest proof of "everything is a plugin": once `forge/_shared/domains/` is empty, the base demonstrably holds no domain.
6. **Then plugin-cs2** — bootstrap stanza, artifacts directory, deduplicated declarations, restored corpus — before it's held up as the reference domain plugin.

Worth keeping as-is: `spec_augmentation.py`'s merge rules, `spec_search.content_root`, and plugin-cs2's own suite (36/36 standalone on an empty `IMG2_HOME`, with a `COLLECTED_FLOOR` integrity test — both checklist items met).

### Open questions

1. Is a `domains/cs2.py` shim meant to ship in-repo, or were the two registry tests left over from an intermediate commit? Decides whether the fix is a new module or a test rewrite.
2. Is `gate_runner` wiring deferred to a follow-up? If so, the wiki's blocking-gate language and plugin-cs2's SKILL.md need a "not yet wired" note now.
3. Which placeholder vocabulary is canonical for `domain.json` — the contract's `{image}`/`{workspace}`, or the base's `{reference}`? Both are in use; neither is validated.
4. Should `--cs2` / `cs2Intake` validation stay as a deprecated path for pre-extraction specs (`append_review.py:409` implies yes), or be removed? The CHANGELOG declares BREAKING while the code keeps both.
5. A generic run writes `objectClass.domain = "generic"`. Intended, or should generic leave the marker unset?

Also: the PR description is still the unmodified template — Summary and Changes empty, all seven checklist boxes unticked. For a BREAKING 68-file change, filling those in would help the next reader a lot.

## Drift items (with file:line + verified evidence)

### DRIFT-1 — EACCES on global npm install
- **Doc says** (`docs/agents/pi.md` line 11-13): `npm install -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`
- **Reality**: On every Linux distro where the user doesn't own `/usr/local/lib/node_modules` (which is most distros — Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora/Arch all have it root-owned), the command fails with `EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '/usr/local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works'`.   ```bash
  export NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX="$HOME/.npm-global"
  mkdir -p "$NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX"
  # add: export PATH="$NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX/bin:$PATH" to ~/.bashrc
  npm install -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent

  2. get a `pi` binary in their PATH
  3. run `pi --version` and get `SyntaxError: 'node:module' does not provide an export named 'enableCompileCache'`
  4. have no idea why

**The same cycle is reported more than once.** `seen_in_cycle` only records the cycle's members. Independent confirmation, with an end-to-end repro on a real 12-component object (kiva fireplace, from a listing photo).

Spec: component `pier-left` with `dimensions {width: 0.42, height: 3.2, depth: 0.56}` and `transform.scale [1,1,1]` — exactly what `new_sculpt_spec.py` scaffolds. `validate_sculpt_spec.py --strict-quality` returns **PASS**.

`generate_threejs_factory.py` (v2.0.1) then emits:

```ts
const mesh_pier_left_1Geometry = endpoint_pier_left_1
  ? new THREE.CylinderGeometry(...)
  : new THREE.BoxGeometry(1, 1, 1, 12, 12, 12);
if (!endpoint_pier_left_1) {
  mesh_pier_left_1Geometry.scale(1.0, 1.0, 1.0);
}
```

All twelve components render as 1 m cubes at their authored centres — the model is a cloud of floating plates rather than a fireplace. Setting `transform.scale = dimensions` on each component (no other change) produces the intended massing immediately.

Two things that would have caught this before I spent a render cycle on it:

1. Apply `dimensions` when `transform.scale` is exactly `[1,1,1]` (the scaffold default), treating scale as an override rather than an authority.
2. Have `--strict-quality` reject any component whose box `dimensions` and `transform.scale` disagree by more than a tolerance, so the failure is loud at validation time rather than visual at render time.

The second matters more than the first: the spec's own metadata says the part is 0.42 x 3.2 x 0.56, so every downstream review artifact believes it is, while the geometry is a 1 m cube.
